settings.headline:
Reporting that
reads between the lines.
settings.copy: The Margin is an independent digital journal covering the stories that move slowly — policy, culture, and the people shaping both. No clickbait, no breaking-news treadmill. Just careful reporting, published when it's ready.

trust_list.text: No paywall on our investigative series

settings.title: The latest
settings.intro: New stories land every week. Here's what the newsroom is working on right now.

features.title: The Quiet Cost of Cheap Water
features.text: A two-year investigation into how a single aquifer is being drained faster than it can refill — and the towns that will feel it first.

features.title: What the Census Missed
features.text: The people who fall through the cracks of every national count, and why their absence reshapes policy for a decade.

features.title: The Librarians of the Last Mile
features.text: In rural counties where broadband never arrived, a small network of librarians is quietly building the internet's last outpost.

features.title: A Field Guide to Slow News
features.text: Why the most important stories rarely break — they accumulate. A manifesto for reading against the feed.

features.title: The Price of a Quiet Street
features.text: How one neighborhood traded its traffic for trees, and what it cost the city in the process.

features.title: Notes from the Archive
features.text: A monthly column digging through old issues to find the stories that were right all along.

settings.title: Reporting that
settings.intro: We don't chase the news cycle. We follow the story until it's ready to be told — then we tell it properly.

steps.title: Pitch and vet
steps.text: Every story starts with a question worth answering. Our editors vet the angle, the sources, and the stakes before a single interview.

steps.title: Report in the field
steps.text: Our writers go where the story is — a courthouse, a farm, a factory floor. We talk to the people who live it, not just the people who tweet it.

steps.title: Edit and fact-check
steps.text: Every piece passes through an independent fact-checking desk. If we can't verify it, we don't publish it.

steps.title: Publish when ready
steps.text: Stories go live when they're done, not when the calendar says so. That's the whole point of a journal that reads between the lines.

settings.note: Our longest investigation took fourteen months from first interview to publication. It was worth every week.

settings.title: Notes from
settings.intro: Short dispatches, reading lists, and the occasional editor's note — straight from the desk.

settings.title: Read by
settings.intro: We don't optimize for engagement. We write for people who finish the article — and they tell us so.

reviews.quote: The Margin is the only publication I read to the end. It doesn't tell me what to think; it gives me the tools to think for myself.
reviews.author: Priya Raman

reviews.quote: Their investigation into the aquifer changed how my town votes. That's not a headline — that's journalism doing its job.
reviews.author: Tom Ellison

reviews.quote: I cancelled three news apps and kept The Margin. It's slower, but it's honest. I trust what I read here.
reviews.author: Aisha Bello

settings.title: One story,
settings.intro: A single long-form story in your inbox each week, plus a note from the editor on what we're working on. No breaking-news alerts, no spam, unsubscribe anytime.

settings.title: Have a story
settings.intro: Tips, corrections, pitches, or just a note about something we got right — we read everything that comes in.

settings.blurb: An independent digital journal covering the stories that move slowly — policy, culture, and the people shaping both.
